speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing neck and arm pain, along with paresthesias and muscle weakness. To help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually, and do they radiate from your neck down to your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.

The patient's chronic neck pain radiating to the arms, combined with progressive hand weakness and paresthesias over a year, strongly suggests cervical spine pathology. Given his age, comorbidities, and the specific pattern of bilateral upper extremity weakness, I need to evaluate the spinal cord compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
